paragraphs.sourceText: 38. In the latter half of the last century, fewer and fewer people believed the basis for our understanding of the world is wholly empirical.

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Research conducted by Jean Piaget in the last century suggested babies were insensitive to others’ thinking.

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Our improved understanding of babies’ intellectual power is attributable to better research tools.

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. It has been found in recent research that even small babies are sensitive to other people’s points of view.

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. With the progress in psychology, the traditional view of children’s self-centered nature and limited thinking abilities has become less and less influential.

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Even though marked advances have been made, it is wrong to dismiss Piaget’s fundamental contributions to the study of kids’ cognitive abilities.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: People often discuss the dangers of too much stress, but lately a very different view of stress is gaining popularity: this view of stress, held by members of the positive stress movement, argues that stress might actually be beneficial. The positive stress movement is made up of people such as
paragraphs.translationZh: 人们经常讨论压力太大的危险，但最近一种截然不同的压力观点正在流行：积极压力运动成员所持有的这种压力观点认为，压力实际上可能是有益的。积极压力运动由以下人员组成：

paragraphs.sourceText: example of followers of the movement. He wakes up most mornings at dawn, goes for a run, sips black coffee while ripping through emails, and then steps into a freezing cold shower. This is a routine designed to reduce the stress of running simultaneously three different health and biotechnology companies for 18 hours a day.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该运动追随者的例子。他大多数早上都会在黎明时分醒来，出去跑步，一边喝着黑咖啡一边翻阅电子邮件，然后进入冰冷的淋浴间。这是一项例行公事，旨在减轻每天 18 小时同时运营三个不同健康和生物技术公司的压力。

paragraphs.sourceText: largely of tech industry workers who claim that such radical tactics will help them live better and longer. Inspired by influential figures in different fields, including entertainers, athletes, entrepreneurs and scientists, positive stress practitioners seek out some combination of extreme temperatures, restrictive diets, punishing exercise routines and general discomfort.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数科技行业从业者声称，这种激进的策略将帮助他们活得更好、更长寿。受到不同领域有影响力的人物（包括艺人、运动员、企业家和科学家）的启发，积极压力练习者寻求极端温度、限制性饮食、惩罚性锻炼和普遍不适的某种组合。

paragraphs.sourceText: Rapp argues that positive stress keeps him balanced. In addition to running and freezing showers, Rapp uses ice baths, hot yoga, and unconventional eating practices such as eliminating dairy, sugar, alcohol and various other foods high in carbohydrates. He believes that these practices, which put stress on his body, actually make him feel less stress from work. However, Rapp does not credit anyone in particular for his choices: he said he started using these methods in college, where he got into the habit of taking ice baths to recover from sports. He got back into it while trying to get his three companies off the ground.
paragraphs.translationZh: 拉普认为，积极的压力使他保持平衡。除了跑步和冷冻淋浴外，拉普还使用冰浴、热瑜伽和非常规饮食习惯，例如不吃乳制品、糖、酒精和各种其他富含碳水化合物的食物。他认为，这些给他身体带来压力的做法实际上让他感觉工作压力减轻了。然而，拉普并没有特别相信任何人的选择：他说他在大学时开始使用这些方法，在那里他养成了用冰浴从运动中恢复的习惯。当他试图让他的三个公司起步时，他又回到了这个领域。

paragraphs.sourceText: Rapp works long hours and sleeps only five to seven hours a night but he said he only gets sick once a year. For him, the difference between day-to-day stress, like the kind we feel when moving apartments, and positive stress is that the latter involves pushing the body to extremes and forcing it to build up a tolerance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 拉普工作时间很长，每晚只睡五到七个小时，但他说他每年只生病一次。对他来说，日常压力（例如我们搬家时感受到的压力）与积极压力之间的区别在于，后者涉及将身体推向极端并迫使其建立耐受性。

paragraphs.sourceText: One thought leader in the positive stress world is Dutch extreme athlete Wim Hof, who earned
paragraphs.translationZh: 荷兰极限运动员维姆·霍夫 (Wim Hof) 是积极压力世界中的一位思想领袖，他赢得了

paragraphs.sourceText: ideas have become popular among tech industry elites and, thanks to Hof, cold showers are now a trend; indeed, some even call it a form of therapy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 创意已在科技行业精英中流行起来，多亏了霍夫，冷水淋浴现在已成为一种趋势。事实上，有些人甚至称其为一种治疗形式。

paragraphs.sourceText: But it is important to note that not everyone agrees with these practitioners; indeed, some medical professionals argue that positive stress is not for everyone, and that it might even be dangerous for people who are unhealthy or older.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但值得注意的是，并不是所有人都同意这些从业者的观点。事实上，一些医学专业人士认为，积极的压力并不适合所有人，对于身体不健康或年龄较大的人来说，它甚至可能是危险的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Is hunting good or bad for the environment? Like so many hot button issues, the answer to this question depends upon who you ask. On the one hand, some say, nothing could be more natural than
paragraphs.translationZh: 狩猎对环境有利还是有害？就像许多热点问题一样，这个问题的答案取决于你问的是谁。一方面，有人说，没有什么比这更自然的了

paragraphs.sourceText: hunting, and indeed just about every animal species—including humans—has been either predator or prey at some point in its evolution. And, ironic as it sounds, since humans have wiped out many animal predators, some see hunting as a natural way to reduce the herds of prey animals that now
paragraphs.translationZh: 狩猎，事实上，几乎所有动物物种——包括人类——在进化的某个阶段要么是捕食者，要么是猎物。而且，听起来很讽刺，由于人类已经消灭了许多动物捕食者，一些人将狩猎视为减少猎物群的自然方式，而现在这些猎物的数量已经减少。

paragraphs.sourceText: On the other hand, many environmental and animal advocates see hunting as savage, arguing that it is morally wrong to kill animals, regardless of practical considerations. According to Glenn
paragraphs.translationZh: 另一方面，许多环境和动物倡导者认为狩猎是野蛮行为，认为不顾实际考虑而杀害动物在道德上是错误的。根据格伦

paragraphs.sourceText: animals...” and is “ irrationally cruel because unlike natural predation (捕食), hunters kill for
paragraphs.translationZh: 动物……”并且是“非理性的残忍，因为与自然捕食（捕食）不同，猎人捕杀是为了

paragraphs.sourceText: of a much larger number of non-game species, resulting in the loss of biological diversity, genetic integrity and ecological balance.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 大量非狩猎物种的灭绝，导致生物多样性、遗传完整性和生态平衡的丧失。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Beyond moral issues, others contend that hunting is not practical. According to the Humane Society of the United States, the vast majority of hunted species—such as waterfowl, rabbits, upland birds and mourning doves—“provide minimal nutrition and do not require population control.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 除了道德问题之外，其他人还认为狩猎不切实际。根据美国人道协会的说法，绝大多数被猎杀的物种——如水禽、兔子、高地鸟类和哀鸽——“只提供最低限度的营养，不需要控制种群数量”。

paragraphs.sourceText: be morally justifiable while others may not be. Hunting “designed to secure the aggregate welfare of the target species, the integrity of its ecosystem, or both ”—what Varner terms “ therapeutic hunting”—is defensible, while subsistence and sport hunting—both of which only benefit human beings—is not.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在道德上是合理的，而其他人则可能不是。狩猎“旨在确保目标物种的总体福利、生态系统的完整性或两者兼而有之”——瓦尔纳称之为“治疗性狩猎”——是有道理的，而自给性和运动性狩猎——两者都只对人类有利——则不然。

paragraphs.sourceText: gathered by the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service in 2006 show that only five percent of Americans— some 12.5 million individuals—consider themselves hunters today, down from nine percent in 2001 and 15 percent in 1996.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国鱼类和野生动物管理局 2006 年收集的数据显示，如今只有 5% 的美国人（约 1250 万人）认为自己是猎人，低于 2001 年的 9% 和 1996 年的 15%。

paragraphs.sourceText: Public support for hunting, however, is on the rise. A 2007 survey by Responsive Management Inc. found that eighty percent of respondents agreed that “hunting has a legitimate place in modern society,” and the percentage of Americans indicating disapproval of hunting declined from 22 percent in 1995 to 16 percent in 2007.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，公众对狩猎的支持正在上升。 Responsive Management Inc. 2007 年的一项调查发现，80% 的受访者同意“狩猎在现代社会中具有合法地位”，表示不赞成狩猎的美国人比例从 1995 年的 22% 下降到 2007 年的 16%。

paragraphs.sourceText: Perhaps matching the trend among the public, green leaders are increasingly advocating cooperation between hunters and environmental groups: After all, both deplore urban sprawl and habitat destruction.
paragraphs.translationZh: 也许与公众的趋势相匹配，绿色领袖越来越多地提倡狩猎者和环保组织之间的合作：毕竟，两者都对城市扩张和栖息地破坏感到遗憾。
